newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss economy to stay in recession in Q1 - UBS.
newsitem.headline: Swiss economy to stay in recession in Q1 - UBS.

text.p: Switzerland's economy contracted further in the fourth quarter of 1996 and will remain in a recession in the first quarter of this year, Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) said.

Based on a quarterly survey of 300 Swiss companies, UBS said all its indicators -- new orders, orders on hand, production -- in the fourth quarter of 1996 were below the level in the fourth quarter of 1995.
"UBS's indicators signal continued recession in the first quarter of 1997," UBS said in a statement.
UBS forecast that Switzerland's Gross Domestic Product fell 0.5 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 and would fall a further 0.7 percent decline in the first quarter of 1997.

Switzerland's third quarter GDP fell by an annualised 0.7 percent in the third quarter of 1996 from both the previous quarter and the year-earlier period, according to Federal Office for Economic Policy.
UBS said there were strong differences between the various industries during the fourth quarter.

Lower production was reported by companies in the clothing, watch, machinery and metals industries, while the chemical/pharmaceutical, food, textiles, paper and electrical industries had higher production levels.
But food, chemicals and textile industries were optimistic about business in the first quarter.
Apart from the watch industry, all industries expect an increase in export orders. This contrasts with expectations for lower domestic orders.
All industries expect to reduce their staffing levels.
The construction industry still considered business conditions to be difficult but confidence had returned to the tourism resorts following the favourable start to the winter season, UBS said.
